rationale: Tests understanding of the four sequential stages of asphyxia, which underpins all subsequent forensic PM sign interpretation.
Tests the important limitation that no single PM sign is pathognomonic of asphyxia — a principle essential for accurate autopsy reporting.
Tests the ability to distinguish smothering from choking based on PM findings and scene evidence.
Tests medicolegal inference in certifying asphyxial deaths — a core applied skill.
Tests the most critical distinguishing PM features of the hanging ligature mark — a core examination topic with precise factual requirements.
Tests the operationally critical rule about never cutting through the ligature knot — a practical skill with direct forensic consequences.
Tests the ability to apply distinguishing features to differentiate hanging from ligature strangulation in a medicolegal scenario.
Tests understanding of the pathophysiological differences between freshwater and saltwater drowning — high-yield differentiation topic.
Tests knowledge of Gettler's test for drowning — a specific and frequently examined biochemical test with a precise criterion.
Tests the practical rule that a body found in water does not necessarily imply death by drowning — a fundamental medicolegal principle.
Tests the ability to identify vital reaction features in burns — the most critical distinction for medicolegal determination of ante-mortem vs post-mortem burning.
Tests knowledge of Lichtenberg figures as a specific and pathognomonic sign of lightning injury — and the critical caveat that they fade.
Tests the medicolegal implications of starvation and neglect — specifically the need to determine whether neglect was causal or contributory.
